question: How did CBA's earnings engine rotate from FY25 to FY26, and was FY26's faster cash-NPAT growth higher quality despite reported NIM compression and a higher loan-loss rate? Reconcile the two years' income/expense/impairment mix with CBA's own FY26 margin bridge.
answer:
CBA's earnings engine rotated from NIM-driven growth in FY25 to volume-driven growth in FY26. Cash NPAT grew 7% ($10,982m, up $730m) vs 4% ($10,252m, up $416m) in FY25. Despite reported NIM compression of 3bps to 2.05% and a higher LIE rate (8bps vs 7bps), FY26's growth was higher quality: it was driven by organic balance sheet expansion (+$92bn AIEA, +8%) rather than liquidity tailwinds, with underlying NIM stable ex-liquids. Operating performance rose 6% ($16,469m vs $15,469m), while LIE rose only $62m (+9%) on a growing book.

**Income/Expense/Impairment Mix:**

| Item | FY25 | FY26 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total operating income | $28,465m | $30,224m | +6% |
| NII | $24,023m | $25,586m | +7% |
| Other operating income | $4,442m* | $4,638m | +4% |
| Underlying opex | $12,866m | $13,585m | +6% |
| Notable items | $130m | $170m | +31% |
| Operating performance | $15,469m | $16,469m | +6% |
| LIE | $726m | $788m | +9% |
| Cash NPAT | $10,252m | $10,982m | +7% |

*FY25 other OI derived as $28,465 - $24,023 = $4,442m.

**Margin Bridge Reconciliation:**

FY25 NIM bridge: Liquids & Pooled Facilities +7bps, Asset pricing flat, Funding costs −7bps, Portfolio mix flat, Basis risk −1bps, Capital/Replicating +9bps, Treasury & Markets +1bps → +9bps total to 2.08%. The 7bps liquids/pooled benefit was a one-off balance-sheet repositioning (RBA TFF repayment reduced low-yielding liquids). Underlying NIM rose just 2bps.

FY26 NIM bridge: Liquids −3bps, Asset pricing −5bps, Funding costs flat, Portfolio mix +2bps, Basis risk flat, Capital/Replicating +5bps, Treasury & Markets −2bps → −3bps total to 2.05%. Underlying NIM (ex-liquids) was stable.

**Quality Assessment:** FY26 growth is higher quality because: (1) NII growth came from +$60bn in average lending AIEA (+7%), not liquidity effects; (2) underlying NIM was stable despite competitive pressure (−5bps asset pricing); (3) LIE rate rose only 1bp to 8bps on a much larger loan book (+$60bn GLAA growth); (4) ETR improved 50bps to 30.0%; (5) ROE rose 50bps to 14.0%. The higher LIE level reflects proactive provisioning for geopolitical risk and macro uncertainty, not deterioration in credit quality.

The chart read (ev-1) shows 'Capital, Treasury & Replicating Markets' as a single bar at +5bps; the text splits this into Capital/Replicating +5bps and Treasury & Markets −2bps separately — the chart aggregation may differ from the textual breakdown.

The question asks whether FY26 growth was 'higher quality' — this involves a judgement call. The evidence supports that growth was more organic (volume-driven vs liquidity-driven), but quality assessment also depends on forward-looking expectations not established in the documents.
